description: No confirmed, robust technical access route into the ESJN notice/award records — the root 403s to a plain client and the open-data endpoint is unlocated.
The ESJN record schema (fields per notice, CPV usage, whether lot-level values and bidder names are published in award notices) was not observed first-hand.
Small-value purchases routed through the e-Пазар marketplace may never appear in the public notice grids, hiding a long tail of POS/terminal/receipt-media purchases.

No enumerated list of payments-relevant contracting authorities (state-owned banks and financial institutions, Фонд за здравствено осигурување, Фонд за ПИОМ, Управа за јавни приходи, Царинска управа, public enterprises, 80+ municipalities) was compiled.
Annual procurement plans (годишни планови за јавни набавки), which flag intended purchases months ahead of a notice, were identified as a source pattern but not systematically located per authority.
Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette) was not examined as a channel for procurement-related legal changes and thresholds.
Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some notices and institutional pages may be published in Albanian; this pass searched only in Macedonian and English.

ESJN (e-nabavki.gov.mk) is an ASP.NET application whose public grids were not exercised in this pass; the parameterised queries needed to filter by contracting authority and CPV for financial services are unknown.

Only central-state buyers were covered; state-owned enterprises and agencies that also buy payment/banking services (e.g. Agency for Financial Support in Agriculture, Employment Agency, Health Insurance regional offices, public utilities) were out of scope here.
No Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed, although MK institutions publish bilingually in many cases.
Archive hosts (arhiva.finance.gov.mk, old.customs.gov.mk, arhiva-cfcd.finance.gov.mk) were identified but not enumerated, so time depth of available award history is unknown.
No URL in this slice was confirmed live; two key hosts failed to fetch from this environment.

Non-bank payment institutions and e-money institutions licensed under the new MK payment services law are not covered by any association member list found; their register presumably sits on the bot-defended NBRSM site and was not retrieved.
Whether ESJN exposes a stable public API or only ASP.NET .asmx/grid endpoints was not established; the observed endpoints suggest scrapable JSON services but this is unverified.
English-language mirrors were only confirmed for MASIT (members-en) and partially for CCC; most registers in this cell are Macedonian-only, and Albanian-language variants were not searched at all.

Only the national chamber (mchamber.mk) and MASIT were mapped; other MK chambers (e.g. Стопанска комора на Македонија/Economic Chamber of North-West Macedonia, foreign investors' councils) were not enumerated.
No source for supplier financial statements (annual accounts) was identified beyond the Central Registry's paid channel, limiting ability to size vendors discovered through award data.
The ДКЖЈН decision register itself was never actually opened — the institutional homepage did not render to a plain fetch and the possible application instance (dkzjn.sorsix.com) was not inspected.

Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although ДЗР brands itself bilingually (Enti Shtetëror i Revizionit) and Albanian-language versions of oversight documents and media coverage likely exist.

Several plausible oversight actors in this cell were not searched: Државен правобранител (State Attorney, represents the state in procurement disputes), Финансиска полиција / Управа за финансиска полиција, Инспекторат / внатрешна ревизија within the Ministry of Finance, and the Комисија за заштита на правото на слободен пристап appeal decisions as a distinct decision series.

Supranational oversight layers were not covered: European Commission enlargement / rule-of-law country reports and SIGMA-OECD public procurement assessments both audit the MK appeals and audit system and quantify its weaknesses.

No archival strategy was identified. Both dkzjn.gov.mk and kzk.gov.mk have visibly restructured over time (legacy 'old.' subdomains, http-only archive years), so older banking-related decisions may only survive in web archives.
The join between an ESJN award notice and its ДКЖЈН appeal case number was assumed rather than verified.

Albanian-language (sq) civil-society and media coverage of MK procurement was entirely out of scope for this run (languages were set to mk and en) and therefore uncovered. Albanian-language outlets and CSOs are a substantial part of the North Macedonian public sphere and monitor procurement in Albanian-majority municipalities.

No commercial tender-aggregation or bid-alerting service for North Macedonia was properly assessed. One such vendor surfaced incidentally (selltostate.com listing an e-Nabavki agency feed) alongside generic 'Balkan tenders' listing sites, but their coverage, freshness and licensing were not evaluated.

Beyond CGK, the depth of the MK procurement-monitoring CSO field is unmapped. Umbrella and directory pointers were found (antikorupcija.mk members page, Civica Mobilitas grantee directory) but their member lists were not enumerated, so smaller and local watchdogs remain unknown.

The actual coverage and freshness of the third-party structured datasets (Opentender MK, opendata.mk databases) relative to the official e-nabavki record was not measured. TED-derived data covers only above-threshold contracts, and MK is not an EU member, so the national-portal-derived share and its lag are decisive but unquantified.

No archival/mirror strategy was identified for the CSO layer. NGO sites and donor-project sites (balkantenderwatch.eu in particular, a project site dating from 2012) are prone to link rot and hosting lapses once funding cycles end.

Albanian-language MK business/finance media (e.g. Portalb, Koha, Zhurnal) were not searched because the run scope fixes languages to mk and en, yet roughly a quarter of the market and several bank branch networks are covered primarily in Albanian.
State news agency MIA and broadcast economy desks (Sitel, Kanal5, Alsat) were not reached in this pass; MIA in particular carries verbatim ministry and National Bank procurement/award announcements.
No MK media archive endpoint (site search API, RSS history, or archive.org coverage depth) was identified, so retrospective reconstruction of past bank technology contracts is currently unplanned.
Sponsored/PR-native content is indistinguishable from editorial on several of these portals, and bank product-launch pieces are frequently supplied by the bank's own PR.

No Macedonian-language term was found in this pass that reliably distinguishes an awarded IT/payments contract from a general product launch; 'договор' alone is extremely noisy (it dominates retail framework-agreement pages such as bank T&C PDFs).

Individual careers-page URLs for most of the ~13 licensed MK banks (NLB, Komercijalna, Sparkasse, Halkbank, ProCredit, ЦКБ, ALTA, Silk Road, TTK, УНИ банка, Капитал банка) were not resolved in this run; only Stopanska banka and MBDP were observed directly.

Supply-side coverage is thin: the local integrator/vendor set serving MK banks (observed only fragmentarily - BCS North Macedonia, Nextsens, Scalefocus, plus international Entrust) has not been enumerated, and their newsrooms and careers pages are not yet tracked. A vendor hiring MK-based implementation consultants is as strong a signal as a bank hiring them.

Non-bank PSPs and e-money institutions (e.g. Iute Pay Macedonia, KEKS Pay) appeared only incidentally. Their licensing, hiring and sponsorship activity was not systematically covered, though they are a fast-growing procurement segment.

Albanian-language sources were not covered at all. A substantial share of MK banking staff and some institutions (e.g. Halkbank, TEB-adjacent networks) communicate partly in Albanian, and Albanian-language MK media and job boards may carry postings and event coverage absent from mk/en channels.
Job ads and conference sponsor pages are ephemeral - postings expire in weeks and event microsites are taken down or overwritten between editions. No archival strategy was established in this run.

The award/recognition angle was only partially explored: international awards (The Banker, Euromoney) were found via MBA, but domestic MK award schemes for banking/fintech innovation - which are typically sponsored by vendors - were not identified.

No Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed, despite Albanian being an official language in North Macedonia and NLB and ProCredit both operating sibling banks in Kosovo where procurement material is published in Albanian.

Parent-side procurement estates for several relevant MK bank owners were not examined: Stopanska Banka (NBG), Silk Road Bank / former Alpha Bank Skopje, Komercijalna banka (now NLB), and the Turkish Ziraat/Halk chain beyond the parent announcements page.

Wayback CDX coverage was probed only for e-nabavki.gov.mk. No capture-index profiling was done for arhiva.finance.gov.mk, the MK bank domains, or the regional aggregators — nor was archive.today (which often captures JS-rendered pages the Wayback Machine misses) tested at all.

Non-EBRD IFI channels were not covered: World Bank/IFC, EIB, KfW/DEG and EU IPA programmes all finance financial-sector and payments-infrastructure work in North Macedonia and each notifies procurement on its own portal, outside e-nabavki.

The two most promising regional aggregators (nabavke.com, ekapija-tenderi.com) are subscription products whose MK depth, historical retention and terms of service were not established. Opentender.eu's data carries a CC BY-NC-SA non-commercial licence.

Supplier-side evidence was not scouted at all — vendor press releases, case studies, reference lists and partner directories are often the only public trace of a closed group framework contract cascading into an MK subsidiary.
nbrm.mk requires a headless/browser-like fetcher; the current toolchain could not retrieve any page from it.
ESJN (e-nabavki.gov.mk) query/API surface not mapped.
The full list of NBRNM-licensed payment system operators and payment institutions beyond MIPS and KIBS is not enumerated.
NBRNM annual procurement plan (годишен план за јавни набавки) documents were not individually located.
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, despite Albanian being an official language in North Macedonia.
IFI/donor-funded procurement channels (World Bank, EBRD, EU IPA) that could fund central-bank or payments-infrastructure projects were not searched.
NBRM's own public procurement page was not located.

Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette) was not searched or confirmed in this pass; it carries the legal acts founding/amending payment-system and procurement rules and some award-related publications.
No open-data / bulk-download channel for ЕСЈН was identified (e.g. data.gov.mk datasets or an ЕСЈН open-data export), only the interactive web UI.

Cell entities beyond the four named ones were not enumerated: e.g. Комисија за хартии од вредност (securities regulator overseeing CDHV), Управа за јавни приходи / Царинска управа (large state e-payment buyers), Пошта на Северна Македонија, and the Interoperability Platform operator inside MDT.
Only one page (kibs.mk news) was actually fetched; all other candidates rest on search-result evidence. Several deep-link URLs given are section roots inferred from observed sub-pages.
No Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed, although MK institutions publish bilingually (e.g. 'ENTI SHTETËROR I REVIZIONIT' appears in State Audit Office headers).

Only Skopje-area buyers were covered in depth (Град Скопје, ЈП ВиК Скопје, ЈСП, БЕГ) plus the two national SOEs (ЕСМ, МЕПСО). The ~80 other municipalities and their ЈКП (Битола, Куманово, Тетово, Прилеп, Охрид water/heating/communal enterprises) were sampled only via one archive example.

Terminology for the specific demand of interest is not yet validated against real notice text: 'услуги на платен промет', 'банкарски услуги', 'ПОС терминали', 'картично плаќање', 'наплатни места', 'фискална апаратура', 'обезбедување и пренос на пари' — none was confirmed against an actual ЕСЈН notice in this pass.
Albanian-language sources were not searched at all. A substantial share of MK municipalities (Tetovo, Gostivar, Struga, Chair, Saraj) publish locally in Albanian alongside Macedonian.

Supplier-side visibility is missing: no register of the banks, security firms and integrators that actually win these municipal/utility payment contracts was located (e.g. Централен регистар company filings, bank corporate/acquiring pages, security-company associations).
No machine-readable interface (API, bulk export, RSS) was confirmed for ЕСЈН; the open-data page 403'd and the PublicAccess portal is ASP.NET WebForms.
Retention limits of the ЕСЈН public front end are unknown; older award notices for this buyer group may only survive in third-party mirrors (Prizma/BIRN) or State Audit reports.
IFC, MIGA and the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) were not covered; CEB in particular lends to Western Balkan financial intermediaries.

Bilateral donors active in MK financial-sector/digitalisation work — SECO/Swiss cooperation, GIZ/BMZ, Sida, USAID successor arrangements, and Austrian/Dutch bilateral programmes — were not individually enumerated.
Award-side transparency registers were only partially covered: the EU Financial Transparency System (FTS) and the EC's beneficiary/contractor listings were not examined.
No CPV / UNSPSC code list has been fixed for banking and payments procurement, so all searching in this cell is still keyword-based and lossy.
Macedonian searching used Cyrillic only; Albanian-language MK sources and Latin-script Macedonian transliterations were not tried.
Historic donor award records (pre-2020 IPA II, closed EBRD/WB operations) were not systematically located; CFCD content is split between a live and an archive host.
Silk Road Banka and Sparkasse Bank Makedonija have no captured annual-report/IR URL in this slice; ProCredit MK has no confirmed tender page despite sister banks publishing them.

No supplier-registration / vendor-onboarding portals were found for any MK private bank, and no group-level supplier portals were confirmed for Erste/Steiermärkische (Sparkasse), OTP/NBG (Stopanska) or Türkiye Halk Bankası (Halkbank).

Because banks publish no award notices, vendor identity must be inferred indirectly; no systematic indirect-evidence channel is yet in the source set (e.g. vendor-side press releases and case studies naming MK banks, ATM/POS certification lists, job ads naming a specific core-banking product).
e-nabavki.gov.mk institution/notice grids are ASP.NET postback-driven and SEI-NET requires per-issuer navigation; neither is reliably collectable with plain HTTP fetches.
Albanian-language procurement vocabulary (thirrje për oferta, prokurim, tender) was not searched for MK banks.
The core-banking supplier for each MK bank is unidentified; no vendor-side reference names an MK core platform (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, ASEE's own core, in-house).
Macedonian-language vendor announcements are thin; Albanian-language sources for MK (a significant local language not in this run's scope) were not searched at all.
The highest-frequency vendor channel for this market (LinkedIn/Facebook company feeds) is ToS-restricted for automated collection, leaving a systematic blind spot.

Fintech/PSP-side vendor evidence (payment institutions, e-money issuers, acquirer-processor partnerships under the MK Payment Services and Payment Systems Law) is not yet covered by any candidate here.
Most concrete MK-named vendor evidence found dates from 2011-2023; little from 2024-2026.
Cash-handling, CIT and security-printing / card-body suppliers to MK banks are entirely unmapped.
LinkedIn 'we won / we delivered' posts — the cell's stated highest-value channel — were only sampled indirectly via search engines, not systematically covered.
The supplier roster is anchored on ~8 well-known firms; the long tail of smaller MK integrators (MASIT's 100+ members, IT.mk IT Index) has not been enumerated.
Global-vendor channel-partner directories were only sampled once (Thales/Nextsense).
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, though a significant share of MK business communication and some suppliers operate in Albanian.
The NBRSM public registers (PI, EMI, PSO, AISP, agents and branches) were identified but their contents were not read due to the 403.
ESJN (e-nabavki.gov.mk) was identified as the A2 backbone but no keyword search of notices/award notices for payment-related subject matter was actually executed in this pass.
Two important actor URLs (kibs.mk for the interbank clearing house, crm.com.mk for the Central Register) were inferred from the entities' names rather than confirmed by a returned search result.
IFI-funded procurement (EBRD, IFC, EU IPA) touching MK payments infrastructure and fintech was not searched; these publish real tender notices where private actors do not.

Vendor-side disclosure was not explored: press releases, case studies and reference lists from POS/switch/KYC vendors naming their MK payments-sector clients would reveal completed procurements from the supply side.
Albanian-language sources were not searched, although Albanian is widely used in MK and some payments actors communicate in it.
